author: "Isaac Neuhaus"

Kaplan–Meier curves summarize time-to-event data: the step-down survival probability over time,
usually split by a group like treatment arm. Here we build one in Python with
[canvasxpress](https://pypi.org/project/canvasxpress/) — it computes the survival steps for you from
a **time** column and a **censoring** column — and the result is interactive and reproducible.

## Install

```bash
pip install canvasxpress
```

## A survival table

Swap this simulated block for your own data: per subject you need a follow-up **time**, a
**censoring indicator** (1 = censored, 0 = event), and the grouping variable.

::: {#855a80cf .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np

rng  = np.random.default_rng(1)
n    = 200
arm  = rng.choice(["Treatment", "Control"], n)
base = np.where(arm == "Treatment", 60, 40)     # treatment survives longer
time = np.round(rng.exponential(base), 1)
cens = rng.binomial(1, 0.3, n)                  # 1 = censored, 0 = event
subj = [f"Subj{i+1}" for i in range(n)]
```
:::


## Build the spec

The two columns — the time and its matching censor flag — go in as the variable samples, and the
arm rides along as a variable annotation. The key is `graphType="KaplanMeier"` and passing **both**
columns to `xAxis`.

::: {#665ebf73 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from canvasxpress.canvas import CanvasXpress
from canvasxpress.render.jupyter import CXNoteBook

data = {
    "y": {"vars": ["Time", "Time-Censor"], "smps": subj,
          "data": [time.tolist(), cens.tolist()]},
    "z": {"Arm": arm.tolist()},
}

config = {
    "graphType": "KaplanMeier",
    "xAxis": ["Time", "Time-Censor"],
    "colorBy": "Arm",
    "title": "Overall survival by treatment arm",
    "xAxisTitle": "Time (weeks)", "yAxisTitle": "Probability of survival",
    "invertCensored": True,               # draw censoring ticks
    "showKMConfidenceIntervals": False,
}

cx = CanvasXpress(render_to="km", data=data, config=config, width=650, height=500)
CXNoteBook(cx).render()
```

Hover any step for the time and survival probability; the tick marks are censored subjects.
canvasxpress derives the survival curve from the raw table, so you never precompute the steps — and
the same spec re-renders the identical curve from R or JavaScript.

## A common gotcha

The survival transform only fires with `graphType="KaplanMeier"`. A bare `"Scatter2D"` gives a raw
scatter of the censor values instead — survival probability is *computed* by the engine, not a
column in your data.
